page: Amazon Web Services c6a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by third-generation AMD EPYC 7R13 processors. Featuring the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled at up to 3.6 GHz. It includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, while offering a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark testing highlights significant multi-threaded computational capability. The c6a.16xlarge achieved top-quartile results in multi-core stress-ng tests (95,671.57), Geekbench multi-core execution (15,953.0), and PassMark CPU ratings (67,169.95). High-throughput parallel routines such as Clang software compilation, ray tracing, and cryptographic operations perform strongly. In-memory data throughput is also substantial, registering 67.6 million Redis SET operations per second and strong cached memory bandwidth, though uncached large-block memory read and write benchmarks operate within the median range. Single-core performance indicators, including single-threaded decompression and compression, settle into standard mid-tier percentiles.

From an architectural perspective, the instance maximizes core density and compute throughput relative to memory capacity. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage represents a tradeoff, meaning high-IOPS applications rely entirely on network storage performance across the 25 Gbps interface. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio restricts applications demanding expansive in-memory state. Consequently, the c6a.16xlarge fits high-performance batch processing, multi-threaded distributed build farms, video encoding, scientific simulations, web serving fleets, and scalable parallel microservices.
description: The Amazon Web Services c6a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and driven by 64 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked up to 3.6 GHz. Utilizing an x86_64 architecture across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, it supplies 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM at a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio, alongside 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system includes zero local storage drives and no dedicated graphics acceleration. Benchmark evaluations place the server in the upper tier for multi-core computation, software compilation workloads, ray tracing, and Redis key-value operations, whereas single-core metrics and uncached memory transfers register at mid-tier levels. With high core density relative to memory capacity, the instance serves as a cost-effective choice for distributed compilation pipelines, batch compute jobs, cryptographic workloads, and horizontally scalable backend services that do not depend on resident local NVMe storage.
